classification.difficultyReason: Use the requested domain comparison to restrict the power law correctly, then recognise symmetry supplies an additional negative branch for ln(x²).

answer.worked:
For $f$, the logarithmic argument must be positive:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&>0\\x&\ne0.\end{align*}$$
Hence $D_f=(-\infty,0)\cup(0,\infty)$.

For $g$, the logarithmic argument must be positive, so $x>0$. Hence $D_g=(0,\infty)$.

answer.worked:
On $x>0$, the power law gives
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\ln(x^2)\\f(x)&=2\ln(x)\\f(x)&=g(x).\end{align*}$$
For $f$, the $x$-intercepts satisfy
$$\begin{align*}\ln(x^2)&=0\\x^2&=1\\x&=\pm1.\end{align*}$$
For $g$, the $x$-intercept satisfies
$$\begin{align*}2\ln(x)&=0\\\ln(x)&=0\\x&=1.\end{align*}$$
Both graphs have vertical asymptote $x=0$ and no $y$-intercept. Their positive branches coincide and increase from $-\infty$ to $\infty$.

Since $f(-x)=f(x)$, reflect its positive branch in the $y$-axis to obtain its negative branch. The graph of $g$ has only the positive branch.
